newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: At least two killed in Colombian bomb blast.
newsitem.headline: At least two killed in Colombian bomb blast.

text.p: At least two people were killed and more than 10 injured in a powerful bomb blast early on Thursday in Colombia's northwest banana-growing region of Uraba, authorities said.

Gen. Ivan Ramirez, the regional army commander, said the bomb, comprised of up to 110 pounds (50 kg) of dynamite and detonated by suspected leftist guerrillas, exploded in the back of a truck parked near police headquarters in the town of Apartado.
"More than 10 people were injured," Ramirez told national radio after confirming that at least two people were killed.

He conceded that the death toll could rise, however, since the bomb practically leveled a hotel in the downtown area of Apartado and caused serious damage to the police station and eight other buildings nearby.
Radio reports, which could not be immediately confirmed, said up to 25 people had been injured in the blast which occurred at about 8:50 local time (1350 GMT).

Ramirez blamed the truck bomb on Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia rebels operating in Uraba. Rebels and right-wing paramilitary groups have been fighting for control over lucrative drug and arms smuggling routes through the region, on Colombia's Caribbean coast near the border with Panama, for more than a decade.
